solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trashy equipment put by school

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Some shoddy gear has been left beside a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes tasteless, cheap-looking art or decor, so it serves as an adjective meaning tawdry.

clue.text: Kick off at home computers, etc, getting cross right away

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
IT is information technology

indicators.note: away tells us the right letter is removed from the angry word

parts.note: cross means angry, as irate does

explanation.surface: Begin with the home computers, getting angry straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start something, the same as to kick off.

clue.text: Untrustworthy like a mule?

definitions.meaning: a ... person is shifty and not to be relied on
a mule is a backless slipper, so mule-like reads as slipper-y

explanation.walkthrough: The mule is footwear, not the stubborn animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery means evasive or unreliable, and jokingly also resembling a slipper.

clue.text: Sorrow shown by a teacher in turmoil after end of skirmish

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the single letter
end of tells us to take only the final letter of skirmish
in turmoil indicates the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Grief displayed by a teacher in chaos once a fight is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turmoil' turns A TEACHER into EARTACHE, which follows H.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a synonym for sorrow.

clue.text: Standard means devised to produce cheese

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: devised suggests the letters of the following word are worked out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Ordinary methods have been invented for making cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Restore grandfather, say, and take a retrograde step

definitions.meaning: literally wind back the hands of a grandfather clock
figuratively to return to old ways

explanation.surface: Reset an old clock and regress.
explanation.walkthrough: A grandfather is a tall pendulum clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom literally means resetting a clock and figuratively means reverting to the past.

clue.text: Staff meet for police operation

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk
a meet is a gathering of a hunt

explanation.surface: Officers gather for a police job.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a meet is an assembly of riders for a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search for a fugitive, typically by police.

clue.text: Rain said to drift in island

indicators.note: to drift suggests the letters wander into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Showers reportedly blowing across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean, an example of an island.

clue.text: Unnecessary medical instruments seen by son

parts.note: needles are used for injections

explanation.surface: Superfluous surgical tools spotted by a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, a direct synonym of unnecessary.

clue.text: A party in action?

parts.note: a party to a legal action is one of the sides suing or being sued, not a festive gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration and 'action' a lively scene, but both are legal terms here.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a person engaged in a lawsuit, i.e. one party to legal proceedings.

clue.text: Crooked group I missed facing French street

indicators.note: missed tells us the letter I is left out of the group word

parts.note: a unit is a group, for instance a military one
rue is the French word for street

explanation.surface: A dishonest gang, one member absent, stands facing a Paris street.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked in the sense of false or not straight matches untrue, meaning inaccurate or out of true.

clue.text: Haste shown in senior policeman's area

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so DI'S is his or hers
a patch is a beat or area of responsibility

explanation.surface: Speed is shown on a detective inspector's beat.
explanation.walkthrough: DI stands for Detective Inspector, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch as a noun means promptness or speed, as in acting with dispatch.

clue.text: A stiff consignment?

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, and consigning one to the earth is an interment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective (a firm delivery) but is the slang noun for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Burial is the committal of a dead body to the grave, a consignment of a corpse.

clue.text: Skip from a slug?

parts.note: a slug is slang for a bullet, and a skip is a bounce off a surface

explanation.walkthrough: The slug is not the garden mollusc but a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is the rebound of a projectile off a surface, a bounce or skip.

clue.text: Boisterous Texan possibly touring university with British royal

indicators.note: touring means the jumbled letters travel around the others
possibly signals that the state native's letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A rowdy man from Texas travelling round a university with a British royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TEXAN into EXANT, which goes around UBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of high spirits, close to boisterous.

clue.text: Group of ladies in drinking session

definitions.meaning: a collective noun for a company of women
British slang for a drinking bout, from beverage

explanation.surface: Women gathered at a boozy get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: The drinking sense is informal British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a flock of women and a session of drinking.

clue.text: European capital? It grows on a troublesome type

parts.note: a bud develops into a flower or leaf
a pest is an annoying person

explanation.surface: A capital city, oddly, where something sprouts on an annoying person.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, an example of a European capital.

clue.text: Feud in event at ground interrupted by leader of district

indicators.note: interrupted by places the single letter inside the jumbled ones
ground, as in milled, means the letters are pounded into a new arrangement
leader of means take the first letter of district

explanation.surface: A dispute at a sports ground is broken up by a local official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' turns EVENT AT into VENETTA, broken by D.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, often between families.

clue.text: Go beyond critical position

definitions.meaning: as in things coming to a pretty ..., a crisis point

explanation.surface: Exceed a dangerous point.
explanation.definitionFit: Pass means to move past or exceed, and a pass is also a critical state of affairs.

clue.text: Lobby for each woman to hold poster

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

indicators.note: to hold means the name goes around the notice

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
an ad is an advertisement or poster

explanation.surface: Campaign for every woman to carry a placard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a noun but is the verb, to press for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to try to influence, which is what persuading does.

clue.text: Dismiss with touch of ridicule outstanding event on school sports day?

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: touch of means just the first letter of ridicule

parts.note: ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Fire someone with a hint of mockery at a fine school event.
explanation.walkthrough: A sack race, hopping in sacks, is a traditional British school sports day event.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a novelty race typical of school sports days, an example of such an event.

clue.text: Inept figure returns with note round university to be determined

indicators.note: returns signals that the word for the inept person is read backwards

parts.note: a loser is an incompetent or unsuccessful person
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A failure comes back with a memo about the university that will be decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firm of purpose, a synonym of determined.

clue.text: Minister going round a nuclear facility

indicators.note: going round places the clergyman around the letter A

parts.note: a rector is a clergyman, a minister of a parish

explanation.surface: A government minister circling a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister is a churchman here, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the installation where fission is controlled, a nuclear facility.

clue.text: A new authority in cathedral characterising a range?

parts.note: a dean is the head of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A fresh senior churchman runs a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The range is the Andes mountain chain of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means belonging to the Andes, the mountain range it describes.

clue.text: In Tokyo, barmen do it as a reminder

definitions.text: In Tokyo, barmen do it as a reminder

parts.words: In Tokyo, barmen do it as a reminder
parts.note: Japanese bar staff stock the rice wine, so they hold sake in store, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as KEEP SAKE: what a Japanese barman does; whole, it is a memento.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small object kept in memory of someone, a memento or reminder.

clue.text: Car from Spain, say

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A car arriving from Spain, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb to state.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is the British name for a station wagon, a type of car.

clue.text: Stories of middle-class country folk, a delightful thing repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the phrase is said twice over

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun, so A GAS

explanation.surface: Novels about well-heeled villagers turn out to be great fun, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga saga is a genre of novel about comfortable English rural middle classes, named after the Aga cooking range.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names novels set among well-off rural English families, so it means such stories.

clue.text: Bear to wander in wood in rest from work

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: to wander suggests the letters of bear roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A bear roams through the forest during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea break is a short pause from work for a hot drink, a rest.

clue.text: Hesitate in start of course before short academic period

parts.note: on a golf course each hole starts at the tee

indicators.note: short says the word for the academic period loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a period of the academic year

explanation.surface: Someone wavers at the beginning of a course, just before a brief term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of course' is not the first letter C: it is the golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to waver or be unsteady, so it can mean to hesitate.
